source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: De quibusdam præambulis in expositione duodecim Prophetarum
1.title_en: On certain preliminaries to the exposition of the twelve Prophets

paras.t: SICUT in novo Testamento evangelicis […] documentis adjuncta est apostolica doctrina, in Epistolis Pauli aliisque septem Canonicis, in Apocalypsi quoque et Actibus Apostolorum contenta, ita in veteri Testamento legi Mosaicæ prophetica dicta ac scripta succedunt : non tamen consimili modo parique causa per omnia. Evangelicæ nempe Christi doctrinæ superadditum est apostolicum dogma : non propter insufficientiam vel imperfectionem evangelicæ disciplinæ ; imo evangelica doctrina prorsus perfecta est, tum quantum ad omnis culpæ exclusionem, tum quantum ad præceptorum et consiliorum evidentissimam traditionem, tum etiam quantum ad exemplaris vitæ exhibitionem, fidei corroborationem, cœlestisque præmii pollicitationem : sed propter particulariorem ac diffusiorem admonitionem ac prosecutionem eorum quæ in Evangelio continentur, et ad præcavendos futuros errores, itemque ad solvendum quæstiones incidentes. Legi vero Moysis prophetia succedit, ut minus dicta suppleat, obscura elucidet, et de Christi mysteriis plenius tractet. Quum enim finis legis sit Christus, secundum Apostolum, in hoc patet imperfectio legis, quod de Christo ejusque mysteriis tam modice tamque obscure profatur.
paras.en: As in the New Testament the apostolic teaching, contained in the Epistles of Paul and the seven other Canonical Epistles, in the Apocalypse also and the Acts of the Apostles, has been joined to the gospel […] documents, so in the Old Testament the prophetic sayings and writings follow upon the law of Moses: not, however, in a like manner and for the same reason in every respect. For the apostolic teaching was added to the gospel doctrine of Christ not because of any insufficiency or imperfection in the gospel discipline; on the contrary, the gospel doctrine is altogether perfect, as regards the exclusion of all fault, as regards the most evident handing down of precepts and counsels, and as regards the showing forth of an exemplary life, the strengthening of faith, and the promise of the heavenly reward: but it was added for a more particular and more extended admonition and pursuit of the things contained in the Gospel, to guard against errors to come, and to resolve questions as they arise. But prophecy follows upon the law of Moses in order to supply what was said too little there, to make plain what is obscure, and to treat more fully of the mysteries of Christ. For since, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 10:4|the end of the law is Christ|finis legis sit Christus]], the imperfection of the law appears in this, that it speaks of Christ and his mysteries so scantily and so obscurely.

paras.t: Denique, secundum Glossam, quemadmodum in corporalis fabricæ constructione tria sunt, quibus ad majora consurgitur, scilicet fundamentum, paries, tectum ; ita et spiritualis structura Ecclesiæ tribus quasi munimentis continetur ac consummatur, videlicet lege, prophetia, Evangelio. Lex ergo quasi lapidem ponit in fundamento, prophetia parietes constituit, Evangelium tectum consummat. In lege enim dicitur : Gentibus multis fœnerabis, fratri autem tuo non fœnerabis. Ecce quasi inchoatio, dum in parte prohibetur usura. In prophetia vero ille fertur in tabernaculo Domini quieturus, qui pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram; et Ezechiel, Usuram, inquit, et superabundantiam non accipies. Ecce profectus. In Evangelio autem dives ille splendide epulans condemnatur, non quia aliena rapuerit, sed quoniam sua non erogavit. Ecce consummatio. Lex itaque elementum est incipientium, prophetia eruditio proficientium, Evangelium consummatio pervenientium : quatenus a fundamento inchoantium, per parietem proficientium, ascendamus ad tectum pervenientium, tanquam cum Apostolo rapti usque ad tertium cœlum, ubi audiamus arcana verba, quæ carnalis homo non percipit. Primum cœlum in lege, secundum in prophetia, tertium in Evangelio. Hi sunt tres panes Eliæ appositi, quos et in Evangelio amicus commodat postulanti. Primus panis est purgatorius, quoniam lex saltem timore pœnæ retrahit a peccatis. Secundus, consolatorius, quoniam prophetia claris de Christo promissionibus consolatur præstolantes. Tertius, consummatorius, quia legis et Prophetarum eloquia Evangelium Christi consummat. Hæc insuper tria, videlicet legalis profunditas, prophetalis subtilitas, evangelica veritas, sunt quasi tria candelabra Ecclesiam illustrantia.
paras.en: Further, according to the Gloss, as in the building of a material house there are three things by which it rises to greater height, namely the foundation, the wall and the roof, so too the spiritual structure of the Church is held together and completed by three bulwarks, as it were: the law, prophecy and the Gospel. The law, then, lays the stone in the foundation, as it were; prophecy builds the walls; the Gospel completes the roof. For in the law it is said: [[Deut 15:6|Thou shalt lend to many nations|Gentibus multis fœnerabis]], [[Deut 23:19|Thou shalt not lend to thy brother|fratri autem tuo non fœnerabis]] [Denis joins Deut 15:6 and 23:19, as the margin shows]. See the beginning, as it were, when usury is forbidden in part. But in prophecy the one who shall rest in the tabernacle of the Lord is said to be he that [[Ps 14:5|hath not put out his money to usury|pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram]]; and Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:17|usury|Usuram]], he says, [[Ezech 18:17|and increase|et superabundantiam]] thou shalt not take[[Ezech 22:12||]] [Denis gives the prophet's words as a command; in Ezechiel they describe the just man, and at 22:12 the sinful city]. See the progress. But in the Gospel that rich man who feasted sumptuously is condemned[[Luke 16:19||]], not because he had seized what belonged to others, but because he did not give away what was his own. See the completion. The law, therefore, is the first lesson of beginners, prophecy the instruction of those who are making progress, the Gospel the completion of those who arrive: so that from the foundation of beginners, through the wall of those making progress, we may ascend to the roof of those who arrive, as it were [[2 Cor 12:2|caught up to the third heaven|rapti usque ad tertium cœlum]] with the Apostle, where we may hear [[2 Cor 12:4|secret words|arcana verba]] which the carnal man does not perceive[[1 Cor 2:14||]]. The first heaven is in the law, the second in prophecy, the third in the Gospel. These are the three loaves set before Elias[[3 Kings 17:6||]][[3 Kings 17:11||]][[3 Kings 17:15||]][[3 Kings 19:6||]], which in the Gospel too the friend lends to him who asks[[Luke 11:5||]]. The first loaf is purgative, since the law at least by fear of punishment draws men back from sins. The second is consoling, since prophecy consoles those who wait with clear promises of Christ. The third is perfecting, because the Gospel of Christ completes the sayings of the law and the Prophets. These three, moreover, namely the depth of the law, the subtlety of prophecy and the truth of the Gospel, are as it were three candlesticks giving light to the Church.

paras.t: Quemadmodum autem ad materialis domus perfectionem atque ornatum alia multa concurrunt, præter tria præfata, videlicet fenestræ, ostia atque solaria, sic ad spiritualis ædificii matris Ecclesiæ perfectionem ac decorem concurrunt præter prædicta, alia multa, videlicet apostolica documenta, de quibus jam tactum est.
paras.en: And as, besides the three things aforesaid, many others go to make up the perfection and adornment of a material house, namely windows, doors and upper rooms, so besides those already named many other things go to make up the perfection and beauty of the spiritual building of Mother Church, namely the apostolic documents, which have already been touched upon.

paras.t: Præterea S. Hieronymus in exordio explanationis duodecim Prophetarum testatur, paucos ante se exstitisse horum Prophetarum expositores. Affirmat tamen se vidisse ac perlegisse commentarios Apollinaris Laodicensis, qui propter nimiam suam brevitatem ad perfectam intelligentiam non perduxit. Origenes quoque, secundum quod refert Hieronymus, parvum super Osee scripsit libellum, in quo omnia quæ contra Ephraim dicit Osee, ad hæreticos refert. Pierius etiam et Eusebius Cæsariensis aliqua super Osee scripserunt. Insuper dicit Hieronymus, quod dum rogatu S. Paulæ esset Alexandriæ, vidit Didymum virum sui temporis eruditissimum, eumque frequenter audivit, atque rogavit ut in Osee scriberet commentarios. Precibus ergo Hieronymi acquiescens Didymus, tres libros super hunc dictavit Prophetam, quos Hieronymus lætabundus recepit.
paras.en: Moreover, St Jerome testifies at the beginning of his explanation of the twelve Prophets that there were few expositors of these Prophets before him. He affirms, however, that he had seen and read through the commentaries of Apollinaris of Laodicea, who because of his excessive brevity did not lead to a perfect understanding. Origen also, as Jerome reports, wrote a little book on Osee, in which he refers to heretics all that Osee says against Ephraim. Pierius too and Eusebius of Caesarea wrote something on Osee. Jerome says besides that when, at the request of St Paula, he was at Alexandria, he saw Didymus, the most learned man of his time, heard him often, and asked him to write commentaries on Osee. Didymus, then, yielding to Jerome's prayers, dictated three books on this Prophet, which Jerome received with joy.

paras.t: Ego quoque nunc opus istud aggrediens, habeo expositionem Hieronymi, Bedæ quoque, qui pauca ponit, nisi quæ sumpsit ex commentariis Hieronymi. Habeo et Glossam ordinariam cum expositione brevissima Nicolai de Lyra. Glossa vero quæ communiter allegatur, intelligenda est Glossa ordinaria: quæ ordinaria dicitur, tanquam regularis et satis authentica, utpote ex sanctorum ac catholicorum patrum sive doctorum dictis collecta.
paras.en: I too, now setting about this work, have the exposition of Jerome, and also of Bede, who sets down little except what he took from the commentaries of Jerome. I have also the Ordinary Gloss with the very brief exposition of Nicholas of Lyra. The Gloss that is commonly cited is to be understood as the Ordinary Gloss, which is called ordinary as being regular [that is, the standard gloss, in common use] and of good authority, since it is gathered from the sayings of the holy and catholic fathers or doctors.

paras.t: Advertendum postremo, quia ut recitat Glossa, S. Hieronymus præsenti libro prologos duos præmittit, quorum primus, qui incipit, Non idem est ordo duodecim Prophetarum, ad totum pertinet librum; secundus specialiter ad Osee : qui prologus incipit, Temporibus Oziæ, habeturque in Bibliis. In primi initio prologi dicit Hieronymus : Non idem est ordo Prophetarum apud Hebræos, qui et apud nos. Unde secundum quod ibi leguntur, hic quoque dispositi sunt. Pro cujus intellectu sciendum, quod Ecclesia usque ad translationem Hieronymi utebatur translatione Septuaginta interpretum. Secundum quos iste est ordo Prophetarum duodecim, Osee, Amos, Michæas, Joel, Abdias, Jonas, Nahum, Habacuc, Sophonias, Aggæus, Zacharias, et Malachias. Ideo dicit Hieronymus, non eumdem esse ordinem Prophetarum istorum apud Hebræos et nos, id est apud Ecclesiam pro tempore illo quo utebatur translatione Septuaginta interpretum. Hieronymus vero ordinando Prophetas, secutus est Hebræos, apud quos ordinantur Prophetæ secundum ordinem quem habent in translatione Hieronymi, qua utimur modo. Propterea modo idem est ordo duodecim Prophetarum apud Hebræos, qui et apud nos, qui translatione Hieronymi utimur.
paras.en: Lastly it must be noted that, as the Gloss records, St Jerome sets two prologues before the present book, of which the first, which begins, The order of the twelve Prophets is not the same, belongs to the whole book; the second specially to Osee: this prologue begins, In the times of Ozias, and is found in the Bibles. At the beginning of the first prologue Jerome says: The order of the Prophets is not the same among the Hebrews as among us. Hence they are arranged here too according to the order in which they are read there. To understand this it must be known that until Jerome's translation the Church used the translation of the Seventy interpreters, according to whom the order of the twelve Prophets is this: Osee, Amos, Micheas, Joel, Abdias, Jonas, Nahum, Habacuc, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zacharias and Malachias. Therefore Jerome says that the order of these Prophets is not the same among the Hebrews and us, that is, in the Church, for the time when it used the translation of the Seventy. But Jerome in ordering the Prophets followed the Hebrews, among whom the Prophets are arranged in the order they have in Jerome's translation, which we now use. Hence now the order of the twelve Prophets is the same among the Hebrews as among us who use Jerome's translation.

paras.t: Osee commaticus est, id est divisus, quia in singulis clausulis diversas vel plenas promit sententias. Idcirco in Prologo scribitur : Et quasi per sententias loquens. Dicitur quoque in Prologo, Osee fuisse synchronon (id est contemporaneum) Isaiæ.
paras.en: Osee is commatic, that is, divided [*commaticus*, from the Greek *komma*, a short clause], because in each clause he brings out different or complete sentences. Therefore it is written in the Prologue: And speaking as it were in sentences. It is also said in the Prologue that Osee was *synchronon* (that is, contemporary) with Isaias.

1.title: EXPOSITIO MORALIS HUJUS PRIMI CAPITULI.
1.title_en: Moral exposition of this first chapter.

paras.t: Jam in superioribus dictum est, quod Osee (qui interpretatur Salvator) figura est Christi, de quo angelus ait : Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum; et Isaias, Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem. Per hoc ergo, quod Deus jussit Osee ut acciperet uxorem fornicationum, præfigurabatur quod Deus Pater dixit Christo, quando misit eum in mundum per incarnationis mysterium, ut acciperet uxorem fornicationum, id est, gentilitatem cum idolis fornicantem sibi desponsaret, atque ex ea exhiberet sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam. Unde et Christus loquitur: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere. In Isaia quoque Pater ait ad Christum : Parum est ut sis mihi ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas; dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. De hoc jam dicta sunt plura.
paras.en: It has been said above that Osee (which is interpreted *Saviour*) is a figure of Christ, of whom the angel says: [[Matt 1:21|he shall save his people from their sins|Ipse salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]; and Isaias: [[Is 45:8|let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem]]. By this, then, that God commanded Osee to take a wife of fornications, was prefigured what God the Father said to Christ when he sent him into the world through the mystery of the incarnation: that he should take [[1:2|a wife of fornications|uxorem fornicationum]], that is, that he should espouse to himself the Gentile world, which committed fornication with idols, and out of it [[Eph 5:27|present it to himself, a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle|exhiberet sibi gloriosam Ecclesiam, non habentem maculam neque rugam]]. Hence Christ too says: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere]]. In Isaias, too, the Father says to Christ: [[Is 49:6|It is a small thing that thou shouldst be|Parum est ut sis mihi]] [[Is 49:6|to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to convert the dregs of Israel|ad suscitandas tribus Jacob, et fæces Israel convertendas]]: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. Of this much has already been said.

paras.t: Porro quod Dominus ait de decem tribubus, Fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino, jam videmus in populo christiano, quomodo aliquorum deus venter est, quorum corda gravantur crapula et ebrietate. Alii avaritiæ (quod est idolorum servitus) student : qui dicunt auro, Robur meum; et obryzo, Fiducia mea : non metuentes quod ait Scriptura, Nihil est iniquius, quam amare pecuniam; et quod ait ad Timotheum Apostolum, Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli. Alii in sophismatibus ac vanitatibus suis jugiter occupantur. Contra quos clamat Joannes : Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris.
paras.en: Further, what the Lord says of the ten tribes, [[1:2|the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord|Fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino]], we now see in the Christian people: how for some [[Phil 3:19|God is their belly|deus venter est]], whose hearts are [[Luke 21:34|overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|gravantur crapula et ebrietate]]. Others are given to [[Col 3:5|covetousness, which is the service of idols|avaritiæ (quod est idolorum servitus)]]: who say to gold, My strength, and [[Job 31:24|to fine gold: My confidence|obryzo, Fiducia mea]]; not fearing what Scripture says, [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|Nihil est iniquius, quam amare pecuniam]]; and what the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationes et laqueum diaboli]]. Others are continually busied with their sophisms and vanities. Against whom John cries out: [[1 John 5:21|Little children, keep yourselves from idols|Filioli, custodite vos a simulacris]].

paras.t: Et abiit et accepit Gomer. Gomer interpretatur consummata sive perfecta. Per hoc itaque, quod Osee accepit Gomer, præsignatum est quod Christus accepit Ecclesiam ex gentibus congregatam, quæ ante conversionem suam fuerat consummata in vitiis, imo in fornicatione carnali et spirituali, eratque perfecta filia voluptatis. Postquam vero ad Christum conversa, et ei in sponsam unita est, facta est consummata in fide, spe et caritate; itemque perfecta in donis Spiritus Sancti, quemadmodum scribit Apostolus gentibus conversis, puta Corinthiis : Gratias ago Deo, quia in omnibus divites facti estis in illo, ita ut nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia. Hinc Salvator hortatur : Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est. Quumque Christus accepisset hanc sponsam, peperit ei filium, qui appellatus est Jezrael, id est, semen Dei. Ecclesia namque per verbum prædicationis et in fonte Baptismatis generat Christo filios gratiæ ac salutis, dicente Apostolo : Per Evangelium in Christo ego vos genui. Quod Ecclesia non faceret, nisi prius cognita atque fecundata esset a Christo, non semine materiali, sed luce cœlesti, donis ac virtute Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[1:3|So he went and took Gomer|Et abiit et accepit Gomer]]. Gomer is interpreted *consummate* or *perfect*. By this, then, that Osee took Gomer, it was foreshown that Christ took the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which before her conversion had been consummate in vices, nay, in carnal and spiritual fornication, and was a perfect daughter of pleasure. But after she was converted to Christ and joined to him as his bride, she was made consummate in faith, hope and charity, and likewise perfect in the gifts of the Holy Ghost; as the Apostle writes to converted Gentiles, namely the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 1:4|I give thanks|Gratias ago Deo]] to God that [[1 Cor 1:5|in all things you are made rich in him|in omnibus divites facti estis in illo]], [[1 Cor 1:7|So that nothing is wanting to you in any grace|ita ut nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia]]. Hence the Saviour exhorts: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]]. And when Christ had taken this bride, she [[1:3|bore him a son|peperit ei filium]], who was called [[1:4|Jezrahel|Jezrael]], that is, *seed of God*. For the Church, by the word of preaching and in the font of Baptism, begets to Christ sons of grace and salvation, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|Per Evangelium in Christo ego vos genui]]. And this the Church would not do unless she had first been known and made fruitful by Christ: not with material seed, but with heavenly light, with the gifts and power of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Insuper Dominus ait : Adhuc modicum, et visitabo sanguinem Jezrael : id est, occisionem seminis Dei, utpote Christi, et aliorum filiorum primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quos occiderunt Judæi, ulciscar, super domum Jehu, id est in populo Judæorum incredulo. Quod post quadraginta circiter annos a Christi passione impletum est, quando Romani destruxerunt Jerusalem ac Judæam, et Judæorum plurimos occiderunt, vendiderunt, disperserunt, et variis modis afflixerunt. Et in tempore illo contritus est arcus Israel, id est, tota fortitudo Judæorum est dejecta in valle Jezrael, id est in humilitate Christi et Ecclesiæ. Christus nempe sua humilitate ac passione promeruit sui ipsius exaltationem, judiciariam potestatem, adversariorum quoque suorum dejectionem. Idcirco superbi Judæi, Christum humilem persequendo, ejus humilitate dejecti sunt. Hieronymus et antiqui expositores, quorum temporibus abundabant hæretici, per decem tribus seu Israel, qui Dominum dereliquerunt, intelligunt hæreticos; per regnum vero seu populum Juda, Ecclesiam. Sicque per contritionem arcus Israel, designatur hæreticorum dejectio, qui Christi virtute vincuntur.
paras.en: Moreover the Lord says: [[1:4|yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezrahel|Adhuc modicum, et visitabo sanguinem Jezrael]]: that is, the slaying of the seed of God, namely of Christ and of the other sons of the primitive Church, whom the Jews slew, I will avenge [[1:4|upon the house of Jehu|super domum Jehu]], that is, on the unbelieving people of the Jews. This was fulfilled about forty years after the passion of Christ, when the Romans destroyed Jerusalem and Judea, and slew, sold, scattered and in various ways afflicted very many of the Jews. And at that time [[1:5|the bow of Israel|arcus Israel]] was broken, that is, the whole strength of the Jews was cast down, [[1:5|in the valley of Jezrahel|in valle Jezrael]], that is, in the humility of Christ and of the Church. For Christ by his humility and passion merited his own exaltation[[Phil 2:8||]][[Phil 2:9||]], judicial power, and also the casting down of his adversaries. Therefore the proud Jews, by persecuting the humble Christ, were cast down by his humility. Jerome and the ancient expositors, in whose times heretics abounded, understand by the ten tribes, or Israel, which forsook the Lord, the heretics, and by the kingdom or people of Juda, the Church. And so by the breaking of the bow of Israel is signified the casting down of the heretics, who are overcome by the power of Christ.

paras.t: Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filiam. Per hanc filiam Osee vel Gomer, quæ vocatur Absque misericordia, designantur hæretici, qui ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis deficiunt, dæmone suggerente, varios inducendo errores, et tanquam effeminati, tentationibus succumbendo. Hanc congregationem seu filiam, quæ divina misericordia meretur destitui, concepit a Christo Ecclesia, dum eos primo fideliter instruit atque baptizat; dum vero fidem rectam et ecclesiasticam deserunt unitatem, efficiuntur proles diaboli. De quibus ait in prima sua epistola Joannes : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis. Hinc Dominus ait : Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel, id est, conventiculis hæreticorum, qui æternaliter condemnantur ; sed domui Juda, id est, Ecclesiæ corde credenti et ore salubriter confitenti, miserebor, perducendo eos ad finem beatum.
paras.en: [[1:6|And she conceived again, and bore a daughter|Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filiam]]. By this daughter of Osee, or of Gomer, who is called [[1:6|Without mercy|Absque misericordia]], are signified the heretics, who [[Luke 8:13|believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|ad tempus credunt, et in tempore tentationis deficiunt]], at the devil's prompting, bringing in various errors and, as if effeminate, giving way to temptations. This congregation or daughter, which deserves to be deprived of the divine mercy, the Church conceived by Christ, when she first faithfully instructs and baptizes them; but when they forsake the right faith and the unity of the Church, they become the offspring of the devil. Of whom John says in his first epistle: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us|sed non erant ex nobis]]. Hence the Lord says: [[1:6|I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel|Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel]], that is, on the conventicles of the heretics, who are eternally condemned; but [[1:7|on the house of Juda|domui Juda]], that is, on the Church, which believes with the heart and confesses unto salvation with the mouth[[Rom 10:10||]], [[1:7|I will have mercy|miserebor]], bringing them to a blessed end.

paras.t: Et ablactavit eam quæ erat Absque misericordia, id est, præfatam hæreticorum collectionem privat Deus gratia internæ refectionis, lacte evangelicæ legis, pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris, quæ malevolam nequaquam ingreditur animam : ita ut tales non jam nutriantur in croceis, sed stercora amplexentur.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she weaned her that was called Without mercy|Et ablactavit eam quæ erat Absque misericordia]]: that is, God deprives the aforesaid gathering of heretics of the grace of inward refreshment, of the milk of the law of the Gospel, of [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|pane vitæ et intellectus]], and of [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aqua sapientiæ salutaris]], which by no means enters a malicious soul[[Wis 1:4||]]; so that such are no longer [[Lam 4:5|brought up in scarlet|nutriantur in croceis]], but embrace the dung.

paras.t: Et concepit et peperit filium. Et dixit : Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus. Per hunc tertium puerum Osee et Gomer, intelliguntur ceteri impii Christiani, qui rebelles sunt lumini, nec per gratiam et prædestinationem attinent Deo, sed sola fide Christiani filiique Ecclesiæ reputantur. De qualibus scriptum est : Ipsi de mundo sunt; et de mundo loquuntur, et mundus eos audit. De quibus ait Salvator : Multi dicent mihi in die illo : Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus, et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, et virtutes multas fecimus? et tunc confitebor illis : Quia nunquam novi vos ; discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis. Istis melius esset viam justitiæ ignorasse, quam cognitam abjecisse : in quibus utique semen Dei non permanet. Horum Deus omnium asserit se non esse Deum, quia nec ipsi eum super omnia amant et colunt, nec ipse per gratiam corda eorum inhabitat, neque per providentiam singularem providet eis efficienter de necessariis ad salutem ; verum dimittit eos, justitia exigente, secundum desideria cordis eorum, ut eant in adinventionibus suis. Quocontra de electis habetur in Apocalypsi : Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eorum Deus.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she conceived, and bore a son|Et concepit et peperit filium]]. [[1:9|And he said: Call his name, Not my people|Et dixit : Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus]]. By this third child of Osee and Gomer are understood the rest of the wicked Christians, who are rebels to the light, and do not belong to God by grace and predestination, but are reckoned Christians and sons of the Church by faith alone. Of such it is written: [[1 John 4:5|They are of the world. Therefore of the world they speak: and the world heareth them|Ipsi de mundo sunt; et de mundo loquuntur, et mundus eos audit]]. Of whom the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:22|Many will say to me in that day: Lord, Lord, have not we prophesied in thy name, and cast out devils in thy name, and done many miracles|Multi dicent mihi in die illo : Domine, Domine, nonne in nomine tuo prophetavimus, et in nomine tuo dæmonia ejecimus, et virtutes multas fecimus?]]? [[Matt 7:23|And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you|et tunc confitebor illis : Quia nunquam novi vos]]; [[Luke 13:27|depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity|discedite a me, omnes operarii iniquitatis]] [the margin gives Matt. vii, 22, 23; the last clause is in the words of Luke 13:27, where Matthew has *you that work iniquity*]. For these it would have been better not to have known the way of justice than to have cast it away once known[[2 Pet 2:21||]]: in them the seed of God surely does not remain. Of all these God declares that he is not their God, because neither do they love and worship him above all things, nor does he dwell in their hearts by grace, nor provide them effectually, by a special providence, with what is necessary for salvation; but he lets them go, as justice requires, [[Ps 80:13|according to the desires of their heart|secundum desideria cordis eorum]], that they may walk [[Ps 80:13|in their own inventions|in adinventionibus suis]]. Whereas of the elect it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and God himself with them shall be their God|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eorum Deus]].
